terms.comment: Masculine (Lewis & Short); Vives’s schoolboys complain of them (Morgan–Owens). Andresian gives it for any bug (see insect).
Traupman’s word, with a long second i; but in Lewis & Short cinifes or sciniphes (with short i) are a stinging gnat of church Latin, not the bedbug.

sources: Lewis & Short: cimex · Lewis & Short: cinifes
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 140, 278.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. bedbug.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
